channel.title: The Bias — Latest news
channel.description: One story. Many angles. Original news, with the context to think for yourself.

item.title: Massie Forces House Action on Hegseth Impeachment
item.description: Thomas Massie reintroduced eight impeachment articles against Pete Hegseth, triggering a two-legislative-day deadline for House action.

item.title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang Faces Inquiries After Admitting Affair
item.description: House committee chairs seek a briefing on Nvidia’s security after allegations of a Chinese intelligence operation.

item.title: Luxon’s National narrowly leads New Zealand election count
item.description: New Zealand’s preliminary count puts National ahead in seats, with special votes still able to change the balance.

item.title: Nithya Raman Unseats Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass
item.description: Bass conceded to Raman, who faces housing pressures, budget constraints and the task of building City Hall support.

item.title: Newsom moves to commute California’s 548 death sentences
item.description: Newsom plans life without parole for 548 condemned prisoners, with most commutations requiring California Supreme Court approval.

item.title: Trump Names Stephen Miller White House Chief of Staff
item.description: Trump chose Stephen Miller to replace Susie Wiles after Republicans lost Congress, drawing criticism from within his party.

item.title: U.S. employers add 165,000 jobs in October
item.description: October hiring beat forecasts and lifted rate-rise expectations, despite rising involuntary part-time work and pressure on pay.

item.title: Democrats Win US House and Senate in Midterms
item.description: Democrats won both chambers in the 2026 midterms, gaining investigative powers while Trump retains his veto.

item.title: Democrats Win Control of U.S. House and Senate
item.description: Democrats are projected to control Congress, gaining oversight powers while facing Trump's veto and Senate procedural limits.

item.title: US launches limited strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island
item.description: Trump voices optimism over Iran talks, but nuclear demands remain unresolved after a round without breakthrough.

item.title: Suspected hackers heat freezers in seven European countries
item.description: Supermarkets across Europe lost food after suspected refrigeration attacks; Ireland's SuperValu disruption has been resolved, Musgrave says.

item.title: Trump Closes Midterm Campaign at Reflecting Pool
item.description: Trump promoted Washington renovations in his final midterm appeal as polls favored Democrats to retake the House.

item.title: Michigan Democrat Haley Stevens Endorses Republican Mike Rogers
item.description: Haley Stevens reversed her Senate endorsement, backing Republican Mike Rogers and prompting staff resignations and Democratic criticism.

item.title: Antonelli becomes Formula One’s youngest champion in Mexico
item.description: Kimi Antonelli secured the 2026 Formula One title in Mexico, becoming the sport’s youngest world champion.

item.title: Anthropic Files to List Shares on Nasdaq
item.description: Anthropic’s IPO filing pairs rapid growth with huge infrastructure commitments, disclosure questions and founder control.

item.title: UCLA analysts challenge Justice Department noncitizen voter list
item.description: UCLA analysts found 8,880 names on the DOJ's suspected-noncitizen list did not match California's current voter file.

item.title: US cancels G20 group photo over Lavrov row
item.description: The G20 group photograph was cancelled after Miliband and other European ministers refused to appear with Lavrov.

item.title: Star Trek actor Sir Patrick Stewart dies aged 86
item.description: Sir Patrick Stewart has died aged 86, prompting tributes to his acting and campaigning against domestic abuse.

item.title: Yorkshire Water chief Nicola Shaw to step down
item.description: Nicola Medalova will succeed Nicola Shaw as Yorkshire Water faces a bonus ban over its environmental rating.

item.title: Apple launches its first touchscreen MacBook Pro
item.description: Apple’s first touchscreen MacBook Pro pairs an OLED upgrade with premium pricing and a familiar laptop design.

item.title: Spain train crash death toll rises to 69
item.description: Spain’s train crash toll rose to 69 as investigators examined a signalling failure and decisions to restart services.

item.title: Alaska governor orders probe over second Dan Sullivan
item.description: Alaska’s governor ordered a probe into alleged Senate candidate recruitment; Peltola’s campaign and the DSCC denied involvement.

item.title: Judge Rejects Trump Bid to Segregate California Ballots
item.description: The Justice Department appealed after a judge rejected its bid to segregate roughly 20,000 California ballots.

item.title: Brazil's Lula wins fourth term in runoff comeback
item.description: Lula secured a fourth term as Bolsonaro vowed an election challenge and Brazilian markets sold off.

item.title: Justice Department Charges James Comey a Third Time
item.description: Prosecutors accuse James Comey of directing a disclosure; his lawyers challenge the case’s legality and timing.

item.title: Microsoft offers voluntary exits to 60,000 workers
item.description: Microsoft’s voluntary exit offer covers roughly a quarter of its workforce, but it expects far fewer departures.

item.title: DOJ seeks conditional block on Alaska certification
item.description: The Justice Department seeks a conditional Alaska Senate certification block, alleging voter confusion; challengers dispute its authority.

item.title: New York Council Backs Horse-Carriage Ban
item.description: New York's council approved a carriage phaseout by 2028, drawing a promised court challenge from the drivers' union.

item.title: WFP cuts food aid to 700,000 Palestinians
item.description: WFP has reduced food assistance for 700,000 Palestinians across Gaza and the West Bank, citing funding shortages.

item.title: U.S. Orders Non-Emergency Staff Out of Saudi Arabia
item.description: Washington ordered non-emergency staff and eligible family members out of Saudi Arabia, citing Houthi attacks on airports and infrastructure.

item.title: iPhone Duo launch brings sellouts and waits
item.description: Apple’s first foldable reached stores with sellouts, as limited supply left some buyers facing months-long waits.

item.title: Meta’s New Shares Preserve Zuckerberg’s Voting Control
item.description: Meta approved non-voting shares as Zuckerberg pledged eight years of residency in California or wherever it is headquartered, conditional on continued full-time leadership and an unforeseen-circumstances exception.

item.title: Meta Ordered to Pay $25 Billion
item.description: Meta was ordered to pay $25 billion over misleading privacy statements, with an appeal expected.

item.title: Russia frees American teacher Stephen Hubbard
item.description: Russia freed American teacher Stephen Hubbard after more than four years; Trump’s claim of a cost-free release drew challenges.

item.title: PHP security flaws trigger widespread precautionary shutdowns
item.description: Public bodies and private services take systems offline over PHP flaws, amid patching warnings and exploitation reports.

item.title: Oman’s Sultan welcomed for UK state visit
item.description: Britain welcomes Oman’s Sultan for a state visit, with investment and maritime-security agreements expected amid regional conflict.

item.title: SpaceX and Tesla Explore a Possible Merger
item.description: Musk says independent committees are exploring a merger, but no transaction terms have been agreed.

item.title: Musk Pledges SpaceX Shares for U.S. Children
item.description: Musk promises children SpaceX shares through Trump Accounts, but eligibility rules and sale restrictions shape the proposed gift.

item.title: Wainwright Fire Kills Four Canadian Service Members
item.description: Four service members died at CFB Wainwright; 39 injured people remained in hospital as officials investigated the fire.

item.title: Trump waives new Russia sanctions and tariffs
item.description: Trump waives new Russia sanctions and tariffs as critics warn the relief could support Moscow's war effort.

item.title: Most Norte Fire Evacuation Orders Remain
item.description: Most Norte Fire evacuation orders remained Saturday after the blaze damaged or destroyed at least six homes.

item.title: Prosecutor: ICE collision witness sent to Mexico
item.description: A witness was sent to Mexico hours after questioning in the ICE collision inquiry, Houston's prosecutor says.

item.title: Suspicious mail targets election offices and lawmakers
item.description: Federal investigators examine nationwide mailings as preliminary tests find no hazardous material and offices face evacuations.

item.title: Hormuz attacks sink ships and disrupt trade
item.description: GFS Pride sank after a Hormuz attack as escalating strikes reduced oil shipments and widened risks for commercial shipping.

item.title: Justice Department sues California over voter citizenship
item.description: The Justice Department seeks to withhold flagged California mail ballots pending citizenship checks; state officials challenge its evidence.

item.title: Russian Strikes Leave Ukrainians Without Power
item.description: Russian attacks leave at least 600,000 without electricity as Kyiv disputes ceasefire claims and questions allied warnings.

item.title: Ukraine reports strikes after Trump’s energy ceasefire declaration
item.description: Ukraine reported fresh energy strikes after Trump announced a ceasefire that Moscow did not confirm.

item.title: Federal Agents Search Ilhan Omar’s Home
item.description: Federal agents searched Omar’s home weeks before the midterms; she accused the Trump administration of political targeting.

item.title: Trump's Russian Diesel Deal Draws Allied Opposition
item.description: Trump's Russian diesel agreement drew allied and congressional opposition as he called for Ukraine to replace Zelensky.

item.title: Riyadh Airport Attack Kills 12, Halts Flights
item.description: Saudi authorities report 12 deaths at Riyadh airport; Trump says the US may join action against the Houthis.
